An artificial intelligence tutor answers questions about a collection of course documents. The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. These datasets must be separated carefully: if passages from the same source appear in both training and testing, the measured performance can overstate the model's ability to handle unfamiliar material. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.

The tutor's language model uses a decoder-only transformer to process text. A tokenizer divides an input passage into tokens, and an embedding layer maps those tokens to numerical vectors. Positional information helps the transformer distinguish sequences containing the same tokens in different orders. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. An attention weight does not establish that the associated claim is true.

Training compares the model's predicted token probabilities with the next tokens in the training examples. A loss function measures prediction error, and backpropagation computes gradients used by an optimizer to update model parameters. The learning rate controls the size of those updates. A learning rate that is too large can make training unstable, whereas a very small learning rate can slow improvement. Overfitting occurs when improved training performance fails to translate into performance on unseen examples. Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly disables some activations during training; ordinary inference uses the trained network without that random disabling. Early stopping uses validation performance to decide when to end training, rather than selecting a stopping point using the held-out test results.

After training, the tutor uses quantization and retrieval-augmented generation for different purposes. Weight quantization stores model parameters with fewer bits, reducing the memory required to store those parameters, although an aggressive reduction in precision can degrade answer quality. Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant course passages when the tutor answers a question. A retrieval encoder maps the question and document passages into embeddings, and a similarity search selects candidate passages from an index. The selected passages are added to the language model's context. Updating this document index can make revised course material available without retraining the language model. Retrieval does not itself change the model's parameters, and a highly ranked passage can still be irrelevant, outdated, or incorrect.

Evaluation must distinguish the quality of retrieval from the quality of the generated answer. Retrieval recall measures how many relevant passages the search returns, while retrieval precision measures how many returned passages are relevant. Neither measure alone shows whether the tutor uses the retrieved evidence correctly. An answer can cite a real passage while making a claim that the passage does not support. The tutor is therefore evaluated for factual correctness, support from the supplied documents, and appropriate handling of uncertainty. When two course passages disagree, the tutor should identify the disagreement rather than combine them into an unsupported conclusion. A failure to retrieve supporting evidence means that support was not found; it does not prove that the proposed claim is false.

relation_proposals.evidence_context: After training, the tutor uses quantization and retrieval-augmented generation for different purposes. Weight quantization stores model parameters with fewer bits, reducing the memory required to store those parameters, although an aggressive reduction in precision can degrade answer quality. Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant course passages when the tutor answers a question. Retrieval does not itself change the model's parameters, and a highly ranked passage can still be irrelevant, outdated, or incorrect.

Prefer one to three words in snake_case; use more words when necessary to preserve meaning. Write a concise reusable definition of the predicate using SOURCE and TARGET. A negative assertion can use the positive predicate with modality='does not'; never omit negation. Keep may/can/usually and similar uncertainty in modality. Keep conditions, exceptions, timing and other necessary participants explicitly in conditions or in a complete endpoint name. Always return conditions and modality: use null only when none is stated. Do not write boilerplate such as certainty or asserts. A temporal phrase, if-clause, purpose or prerequisite belongs in conditions. Endpoints name standalone concepts including processes and properties, not whole assertions. Preserve each participant's owner and scope; a property, change in that property and its owner are distinct concepts. Use causal predicates only when the source states causation. Split conjunctions into their distinct assertions without losing their shared conditions. Abstract examples only: 'ConceptA may influence ConceptB under ConditionC' gives ConceptA -> influences -> ConceptB, modality='may', conditions='under ConditionC'. 'PropertyQ does not establish ProcessP' gives PropertyQ -> establishes -> ProcessP, modality='does not'. Never copy these placeholders. A leading definite article alone does not make a name an unresolved reference: 'the ConceptA' can be named 'ConceptA'. Resolve pronouns and demonstratives anywhere inside a name, including its, their, them, and those, using the supplied sentences. Replace each reference with its text-supported antecedent while preserving the full concept, its owner, and its scope. If ConceptA has parts, 'the structure of its parts' can become 'structure of ConceptA's parts'; do not reduce it to ConceptA or to parts. The quote may include supplied adjacent text when needed to resolve references. Capture the literal direction and degree of support; do not strengthen an association into causation or a possibility into certainty. Do not infer unstated background facts. A claim without a relationship is appropriate only if a faithful connection genuinely cannot express it; lack of an existing predicate is never a reason. {"chunks": [{"id": "chunk_002", "text": "The tutor's language model uses a decoder-only transformer to process text. A tokenizer divides an input passage into tokens, and an embedding layer maps those tokens to numerical vectors. Positional information helps the transformer distinguish sequences containing the same tokens in different orders. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. An attention weight does not establish that the associated claim is true."}]}

A loss function measures prediction error, and backpropagation computes gradients used by an optimizer to update model parameters. The learning rate controls the size of those updates. A learning rate that is too large can make training unstable, whereas a very small learning rate can slow improvement. Overfitting occurs when improved training performance fails to translate into performance on unseen examples. Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly disables some activations during training; ordinary inference uses the trained network without that random disabling. Early stopping uses validation performance to decide when to end training, rather than selecting a stopping point using the held-out test results."}]}

{"chunks": [{"id": "chunk_004", "text": "After training, the tutor uses quantization and retrieval-augmented generation for different purposes. Weight quantization stores model parameters with fewer bits, reducing the memory required to store those parameters, although an aggressive reduction in precision can degrade answer quality. Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant course passages when the tutor answers a question. A retrieval encoder maps the question and document passages into embeddings, and a similarity search selects candidate passages from an index. The selected passages are added to the language model's context. Updating this document index can make revised course material available without retraining the language model. Retrieval does not itself change the model's parameters, and a highly ranked passage can still be irrelevant, outdated, or incorrect."}]}

First enumerate each separate source assertion in claims, then cite the graph edges that express that assertion and write their actual combined reading. Conditions and definitions cannot supply an absent action or argument unless it is actually saved in those fields. A relation to a bare participant does not convey what that participant does. Read predicates literally with their conditions and modality: modality outside the parentheses applies to the whole assertion, so NOT (A R B) does not mean A R (NOT B). Cite exact source_sentence_ids instead of copying quotations; include adjacent IDs when needed to resolve references. For unsupported entries also copy the exact graph edge id. Give concise conclusions, never a reasoning transcript. Return one result under each supplied item ID.

Represent every substantive assertion as one or more directed source-predicate-target relationships. Predicates are OPEN VOCABULARY: write the verb or phrase that accurately expresses the source. Prefer one to three words in snake_case; use more words when necessary to preserve meaning. Write a concise reusable definition of the predicate using SOURCE and TARGET. A negative assertion can use the positive predicate with modality='does not'; never omit negation. Keep may/can/usually and similar uncertainty in modality. Keep conditions, exceptions, timing and other necessary participants explicitly in conditions or in a complete endpoint name. Always return conditions and modality: use null only when none is stated. Do not write boilerplate such as certainty or asserts. A temporal phrase, if-clause, purpose or prerequisite belongs in conditions. Endpoints name standalone concepts including processes and properties, not whole assertions. Preserve each participant's owner and scope; a property, change in that property and its owner are distinct concepts. Use causal predicates only when the source states causation. Split conjunctions into their distinct assertions without losing their shared conditions. Abstract examples only: 'ConceptA may influence ConceptB under ConditionC' gives ConceptA -> influences -> ConceptB, modality='may', conditions='under ConditionC'. 'PropertyQ does not establish ProcessP' gives PropertyQ -> establishes -> ProcessP, modality='does not'. Never copy these placeholders. A leading definite article alone does not make a name an unresolved reference: 'the ConceptA' can be named 'ConceptA'. Resolve pronouns and demonstratives anywhere inside a name, including its, their, them, and those, using the supplied sentences. Replace each reference with its text-supported antecedent while preserving the full concept, its owner, and its scope. If ConceptA has parts, 'the structure of its parts' can become 'structure of ConceptA's parts'; do not reduce it to ConceptA or to parts. The quote may include supplied adjacent text when needed to resolve references. Capture the literal direction and degree of support; do not strengthen an association into causation or a possibility into certainty. Do not infer unstated background facts. Relation endpoints need not also be repeated in concepts. Return all substantive relationships without a count quota. Give a short conclusion in reason. Preserve negation, uncertainty, conditions and full participant meanings. Do not add background knowledge or merely restate already represented claims.

The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. Overfitting occurs when improved training performance fails to translate into performance on unseen examples. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.

source_context.text: An artificial intelligence tutor answers questions about a collection of course documents. The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. These datasets must be separated carefully: if passages from the same source appear in both training and testing, the measured performance can overstate the model's ability to handle unfamiliar material. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.

During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.

source_context.text: An artificial intelligence tutor answers questions about a collection of course documents. The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. These datasets must be separated carefully: if passages from the same source appear in both training and testing, the measured performance can overstate the model's ability to handle unfamiliar material. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.
